description:
FILED AND SHIPPED s463av (round 20 perf slot), as the "profile the worst
lagging row" task.  The row chosen was `slices` (the highest pcl/perl ratio
with a runtime-side cause once pack/packunpk (#74), ovlsub (#582) and regexg
(#71) are excluded): 3.05x at the round's base.

THE PROFILE (sb-sprof, :cpu, 0.5 ms, N = 1.5e6, 1492 samples, base tree; the
row is `my @a=(1..50); my %h = map {$_=>$_} 1..50; my @k=(1..10);` then
`my @v = @a[1..5]; my @w = @h{@k}` in a loop):

     self%  total%  function
      11.7    20.6  sb-impl::gethash/equal
       7.4    26.9  (labels add-items :in p-array-fill)
       5.0    47.5  p-hslice
       4.8     7.6  %p-fixnum-string
       3.6     8.8  sb-vm::reallocate-vector-with-widetag
       3.4    13.4  p-aslice
       3.2     3.2  sb-kernel:%set-fill-pointer
       3.1    11.8  sb-vm::extend-vector
       3.1     3.1  unbox
       2.9     6.1  p-aref-argbox
       2.5    19.5  %p-array-store-scalar
       2.4    33.3  %p-alias-helem
       2.3     2.3  sb-kernel:string=*
       1.6     2.4  %p-snapshot-array-rhs
       1.3    16.1  vector-push-extend
       1.0    30.9  p-array-fill

Three groups: the hash machinery ~21 % (gethash/equal with sxhash-string,
string=* and equal under it), key stringification ~9 % (%p-fixnum-string +
to-string + stringify-value — task #982, and it has a hazard that must be
answered before anything is done about it), and VECTOR GROWTH 16.1 %
(vector-push-extend -> extend-vector 11.8 -> reallocate 8.8, plus
%set-fill-pointer 3.2).

THE GROWTH WAS REAL AND ITS CAUSE IS EXACT.  `my @v` inside a loop emits
`(make-array 0 :adjustable t :fill-pointer 0)` EVERY iteration, so p-array-fill
pushed five elements into a zero-capacity vector and walked a full doubling
sequence — re-discovering, one reallocation at a time, a length the source
already knew.  p-aslice, p-hslice and %p-snapshot-array-rhs had all been sized
already (s458ak); p-array-fill was the one left.

THE FIX: `%p-fill-lower-bound` (string -> 1, hash-table -> 2 x count, vector or
list -> its length, else 1) and one reservation in p-array-fill after the fill
pointer is cleared, growing PLACE's capacity only when it is short.  It is a
LOWER bound because add-items recurses (a nested vector or hash expands past
it); a bound that is too small merely costs what today costs always.  Capacity
is invisible to Perl, and the reservation only ever grows, so a reused array in
a loop adjusts at most once.  ADJUSTABLE-ARRAY-P is checked because
`adjust-array` on a non-adjustable array returns a FRESH array and leaves the
original alone — unguarded, that would silently drop the whole assignment.

THE MEASUREMENT, AND THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING: **the profile's 16 % is NOT
the prize.**  Re-profiling with the fix in shows the growth family gone from
the top and `adjust-array` in its place at 11.1 % total (with `replace` 3.2 %
under it) — `adjust-array` allocates and copies too, so most of the growth cost
is merely relocated.  What is left is small, and the bench row's own A/B says
so: six interleaved best-of-5 samples on the array rows give

    slices    +0.9 % median  (-0.2 +2.9 +1.0 +0.8 -0.5 +4.3)
    sliceasgn +1.6 %         (-5.3 +2.0 +1.7 +0.5 +1.5 +6.9)
    arrfill   +0.4 %   arrhash -0.6 %   feread -0.2 %

(positive = the tree WITHOUT the reservation is slower, i.e. the fix helps).
~1 % on the two slice rows, nothing elsewhere.  Had that been the whole story
this would have been a recommend-decline like #883 and #924.

IT IS NOT, AND THE BENCH WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT.  Both slice rows assign 5
and 10 elements — too few for the growth to matter against their hash traffic.
On an ordinary whole-array copy, interleaved best-of-5, startup subtracted:

    my @c = @src, @src = 1..50    (1e6 copies)   A 0.610 s  B 0.735 s   +20.4 %
    my @c = @src, @src = 1..2000  (2e5 copies)   A 3.884 s  B 4.281 s   +10.2 %
                                       repeat:   A 3.826 s  B 4.302 s   +12.4 %

So the fix is worth **10-20 % of the commonest list assignment there is**, and
the reason nobody had seen it is that no bench row covered the shape.  s463av
added one: `listcopy` (50 elements x 1e6), which reads **0.89x — PCL beats
perl** on it.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, with its measurement, so the next session does not re-derive
it: `%p-flatten-slice-args` builds a throwaway LIST per slice call
(`coerce ... 'list` + `append`), which the same profile puts at ~5 % of the
`slices` row (vector-to-list 2.6 %, copy-list-to 2.1 %).  The single-vector
case — `@a[1..5]`, `@h{@k}`, i.e. every slice the corpus writes — could iterate
the argument vector directly.  Six callers share the helper, so the change is a
representation change across all of them, not a fast arm in two (rule 11).
Filed as **#985**.
subject: Perf: p-array-fill re-discovered the destination's length one growth at a time — `my @c = @src` is 20 % faster with the capacity reserved (SHIPPED s463av)
